svg.title: ai-gateway integration architecture
svg.desc: An existing application keeps its front end, backend, orchestration and tools; only its LLM client layer changes to call the ai-gateway service, which classifies, caches, budgets and routes to small, mid and frontier model backends, and plugs into identity, secrets, Redis, observability, SIEM and finance systems.
svg.text: ai-gateway: integrating with an existing application
One client-layer change in the app; everything else plugs in behind the gateway
Dashed: needs real infrastructure, or not run here
Existing or new. Its result becomes the X-Sensitivity
LLM client layer: the only change
Was: model='gpt-4o', calling the provider directly.
Adds headers: X-App-Id, X-Agent, X-Run-Id (same for every
step of a run), X-Step, X-Sensitivity.
Reads app, agent, run, step, sensitivity from headers (or body
Size score picks a tier; tools bump small to mid; sensitive
Calls with no tools at temperature 0 or near it. A hit is free
App daily budget plus per-run budget and step cap. Over
Reads real token usage and trues up the estimated cost.
OpenAI-shaped body plus X-AI-Gateway-* headers: tier, cost,
CPU clusters (quantized models) and small GPU clusters. Simple
13B to 70B class open models. Most day-to-day work, including
OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI or Bedrock. Reserved for the
hardest requests. Never receives sensitive data.
The prototype uses mock models. Real calls need an
OPENAI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and real clusters.
ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS THE GATEWAY PLUGS INTO
Virtual key per app, linked to
Showback by app and cost per
1. Point each agent's client at the gateway: base_url and key.
2. Use model 'ai-gateway/auto' instead of a fixed model (pin a tier only where needed).
3. Tag calls: X-App-Id, X-Run-Id (reuse across the run), X-Step.
4. Set X-Sensitivity from your PII check.
5. Handle 429 (budget spent) and 403 (policy conflict): stop or degrade, never retry.
6. Re-run each agent's quality evaluations, because routing changes which model answers.
Your application logic, user-facing APIs and sessions.
The orchestration graph: nodes, edges, state.
Your tools, databases and internal APIs.
How agents are written: still the standard OpenAI-style client call.
Rollback: point base_url back at the provider.
Reference architecture. Verified against the mock backend; production items (dashed) are not built or not run in the prototype.
